desc: Read input $N, K$ and the tree edges, then build an adjacency list representation of the tree.
Implement a recursive DFS function that traverses the tree in post-order (bottom-up) to calculate component sizes.

Inside the DFS, for each node, sum the sizes of valid components returned by its children. If a child returns a component of size $K$, increment the global path counter and treat that child's contribution as 0 (path cut).
If at any point the accumulated size at a node exceeds $K$, immediately return "No" and terminate.
After the DFS completes, check if the global path counter equals $N$ and the size of the component at the root is exactly 0 (meaning all nodes were perfectly partitioned).
Print "Yes" if conditions are met, otherwise print "No".
Verify the logic with Sample 1 and Sample 2 manually or mentally.
Ensure edge cases like $K=1$ or $N=1$ are handled (code handles $K=1$ explicitly).
Confirm the output format matches exactly ("Yes" / "No").
Run the provided code against Sample 1 and Sample 2 to verify correctness.
Test with edge cases (e.g., N=1, K=large; Star graph; Line graph).
If all tests pass, mark as solved.
